samples.summary: Always materializing `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on the caret silently overrides the documented asymmetric range-start default, changing selection-highlight behaviour beyond the issue's scope
samples.evidence: `moveTo`/constructor now stamp `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on every caret position (cursor.ts:26,55). Keyboard shift-selection uses the caret as the anchor when no range exists (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos` — text-editor.ts:2774; also handleHome text-editor.ts:2807). `buildRects` documents and relies on the asymmetric default `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (selection.ts:260-261, mirrored in the DocPosition docblock model/types.ts:204-208 and in docs-local-caret-anchoring.md's 'A standalone caret keeps the historical backward reading'). Previously a keyboard-derived caret carried no affinity, so a wrap-boundary anchor read 'forward' as a range start; now it arrives as an explicit 'backward', so the highlight can open on a zero-width sliver of the previous visual line — the exact failure that default exists to prevent. The design-doc hunk asserts 'absent stays reserved for endpoints from other producers', but caret-derived anchors are precisely one of those endpoints, so the invariant is asserted rather than preserved. Nothing in the change's stated goal (caret affinity reaching presence / peer caret rendering) requires making the caret's default explicit.

samples.summary: `resolvePositionPixel` now keeps two sources of truth for affinity (a required-but-undefined-able positional param plus `position.lineAffinity`), reintroducing the ambiguity the change is meant to remove
samples.evidence: Signature becomes `lineAffinity: 'forward' | 'backward' | undefined` with an internal fallback `lineAffinity ?? position.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'` (peer-cursor.ts:105,111), while every in-repo caller now just forwards the position's own field (editor.ts:1570, editor.ts:2823, cursor.ts:74). The param is still positionally required, so callers must pass `undefined` or re-read the field they already have. Making it an optional trailing override (or dropping it where it is redundant) would leave one home for the value, matching the change's own 'single home for caret affinity' framing.

samples.summary: The presence wire type still redeclares the position/range shape inline instead of reusing `DocPosition`/`DocRange`, which is the duplication the diff blames for the affinity falling off the wire
samples.evidence: `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos` and `activeSelection.anchor/.focus` are hand-written `{ blockId; offset; lineAffinity? }` literals (users.ts:21-37) even though the diff standardized the store (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2879,2901,2917,2978) and the editor API (editor.ts:128,1182) on the shared `DocPosition`/`DocRange` types from @wafflebase/docs, which frontend already imports. Leaving a parallel structural copy of the same shape at the wire boundary is the same reuse gap that let a narrower type drop the field; frontend has no `tsc` lane, so a future divergence here is unchecked.

samples.summary: Six copies of the same inline structural cast for the optional store hooks were edited instead of consolidated into one shared optional-store interface
samples.evidence: The diff updates the identical `(docStore as { setCursorForHistory(pos: DocPosition, selection?: DocRange | null): void })` literal at editor.ts:1013, 1116, 1953, 2162, 2991, plus two `getPresenceCursorPos` casts at 2026/2058. Touching all seven in one change is the natural moment to declare a single `PresenceCapableDocStore` (or optional members on `DocStore`), which would also make the next type widening a one-line change rather than a seven-site sweep.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is genuinely present (cursor.ts:26,55 materialize `lineAffinity: 'backward'`; text-editor.ts:2774,2807 use the caret as the shift-selection anchor; selection.ts:260-261 applies the asymmetric start/end default), so this is not a `not-present` refutation. But the finding is framed as a design-fit defect ("beyond the issue's scope", "invariant asserted rather than preserved"), and on that lane it fails. The originating issue's own approach section mandates exactly this: "A caret position always states its reading (materialized, defaulting to 'backward')" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:29-31), with the matching step at :39-40 and the acceptance criterion "Home / arrow carets publish an affinity (not just mouse clicks)" at :60 — which cannot be satisfied for the `moveTo(newPos)` no-affinity keyboard paths (text-editor.ts:2831, :2846) without materialization. So it is the specified approach, not unrequested scope creep, and no acceptance criterion is left unmet. Design-doc discipline is also satisfied: the change folded into the canonical subsystem docs (docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:89-101, docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:189-203) rather than adding a parallel doc, and those docs explicitly state the affinity is meant to travel "into presence, undo history, selection endpoints and rendering", so the selection-endpoint consequence is an intended documented effect. No duplicated module or stated Non-Goal is implicated. What remains is a line-level rendering-behaviour question about whether a backward-affinity anchor emits an extra rect at a wrap boundary (selection.ts:415-429) — the correctness lens's lane, explicitly deferred by this rubric, and already logged there as minor (.agent-review/correctness/verdict.json:4-10). Under the design-fit rubric this is at best a `minor` approach preference, which never blocks.
